item.title: Python Name Mangling Explained: Why Double Underscore Members Aren't Truly Private
item.description:
“Python Name Mangling Explained: Why Double Underscore Members Aren’t Truly Private”

In object-oriented programming, the concept of private members is central to encapsulation, protecting internal states from external tampering. However, Python treats this concept differently than strictly enforced languages like Java or C#. What is the technical reality behind Python identifiers prefixed with a double underscore (e.g., __variable or __method)? Are they genuinely inaccessible, and what is the mechanism Python employs?

item.title: Python Parent Method Calling Techniques: Super() vs Direct Access
item.description:
“Python Parent Method Calling Techniques: Super() vs Direct Access”

When dealing with inheritance in object-oriented Python programming, a common requirement arises: how does a child class correctly invoke a method defined in its parent class, especially when that method has been overridden? While the super() function is the modern standard, several techniques exist, differing based on Python versions and specific inheritance scenarios (like multiple inheritance). This deep dive examines these diverse approaches for accessing parent functionality.
